H4KS02164.name: Derek Schmidt
H4KS02164.bio: U.S. Representative for Kansas' 2nd District since 2025; former Kansas Attorney General for 12 years.

positions.stance: Cosponsored and passed the Laken Riley Act and Sarah's Law to protect communities from the consequences of the Biden-era border crisis.
Fighting to curb runaway federal spending, lower inflation, and extend tax relief for Kansas families, small businesses, farmers and ranchers.
Leading legislation to support victims of violent crime, coordinate the federal response to scams targeting seniors, and deport non-citizen fraudsters.

H6KS02276.name: Don Coover
H6KS02276.bio: U.S. Army veteran and former military intelligence officer and pilot; veterinarian who runs a beef cattle genetics company and ranch.

H8KS03155.name: Sharice Davids
H8KS03155.bio: U.S. Representative for Kansas' Third Congressional District.

positions.stance: Committed to ensuring farmers, ranchers, and producers have the tools to succeed, including reliable crop insurance, agricultural research, and access to nutritious food.
Committed to making education more accessible and affordable, and to apprenticeships, technical training, and STEM programs for the jobs of tomorrow.
Believes "we can tackle climate change while unlocking the economic opportunities of clean energy," including Kansas wind and renewable energy.
Dedicated to reducing big money in politics, strengthening ethics laws, and keeping elections "free, fair, and accessible to all."
Supports common-sense, bipartisan gun safety measures that respect responsible gun ownership, and resources and training for local law enforcement.

H6KS03308.name: Eric Jenkins
H6KS03308.bio: Retired U.S. Army Colonel, FEMA career professional, and former Shawnee City Council president.

positions.stance: Opposes deficit spending, supports a balanced budget framework, and wants the Trump-era tax cuts extended and made permanent.
Supports fully funding and modernizing the military, veterans' healthcare and benefits, and opposes "reckless foreign entanglements."
Supports completing a secure southern border, ending catch-and-release, and defunding cities that obstruct federal immigration enforcement.
Supports reducing regulations on businesses and farmers, American energy independence, and fair trade deals; opposes the Green New Deal.
Pledges to defend Second Amendment rights, free speech, and religious liberty, and supports appointing constitutionalist judges.

H8KS04112.name: Ron Estes
H8KS04112.bio: U.S. Representative for Kansas' Fourth District on the Ways and Means Committee; former Kansas State Treasurer and Sedgwick County Treasurer.

positions.stance: Will never support the federal government taking power from the people, and describes himself as "proudly pro-life."
Committed to rolling back burdensome regulations and out-of-control spending, and supports free and fair trade for Kansas farmers.
Supports securing the border, more tankers for McConnell Air Force Base, and pay raises for troops.
Supports Make America Healthy Again efforts, rural health funding, and health care price transparency.
Supports limiting the federal government, rolling back unnecessary regulations, and giving more power to Kansans and local governments.

H6KS04272.name: Katy Tyndell
H6KS04272.bio: Attorney and business owner; former staff attorney for the National Congress of American Indians.

positions.stance: Will work to ensure access to quality, affordable healthcare for all, including affordable, accessible mental health services.
Will stand up for working people and small businesses, work to lower taxes on working Kansans, and bring both parties together to drive costs down.
Will fight to reverse tariff policies hurting Kansas agriculture and oppose industrial encroachment and pesticide deregulation.
Will bring both parties together "to ensure the future of AI is a job creator, not a job killer."
Will champion legislation to protect people's privacy online, especially youth, so tech giants cannot endlessly mine personal data.

H2NM01144.name: Melanie Stansbury
H2NM01144.bio: U.S. Representative for New Mexico's First Congressional District since 2021; former New Mexico state representative.

positions.stance: Focused on expanding the economy, supporting local businesses, and growing more meaningful jobs.
Champions investments in broadband, drinking water, roads, and more resilient and sustainable infrastructure.
Supports raising the federal minimum wage to $15 an hour.
Supports humane immigration policies, reuniting families, and a path to citizenship.
Works to get big money out of politics, supports campaign finance reform, and does not accept corporate or corporate PAC funds.

wiki:didi-okapareke.name: Didi Okapareke
wiki:didi-okapareke.bio: Pharmacist and owner of Olive Tree Compounding Pharmacy in Albuquerque.

positions.stance: Will work to make healthcare affordable and accessible for every New Mexico family, lowering costs at the pharmacy counter and expanding access.
Will fight to bring federal investments and programs to New Mexico that create jobs and grow paychecks: "Prosperity instead of poverty."
Will "vote for what is right for our families and our communities, every single time, no matter who it upsets."

H2NM02191.name: Gabe Vasquez
H2NM02191.bio: U.S. Representative for New Mexico's 2nd District; former Las Cruces City Councilor.

positions.stance: Supports raising wages, the PRO Act, small businesses, repealing the Trump tax cuts, and cutting taxes for working families.
Founded the Bipartisan Public Lands Caucus to protect New Mexicans' ability to hunt, fish, and hike on public lands.
Working across the aisle to crack down on cartels, keep them from recruiting kids, and get illegal guns off the streets.
Supports reversing Republican health care cuts, a public option, Medicare drug price negotiation, and capping insulin prices.
Supports commonsense border security, deporting violent criminals, reforming ICE, protecting DREAMers, and a path to legal status.

H6NM02127.name: Greg Cunningham
H6NM02127.bio: Marine Corps combat veteran, former Albuquerque police officer, and business owner.

H0NM03102.name: Teresa Leger Fernández
H0NM03102.bio: U.S. Representative for New Mexico's Third Congressional District.

positions.stance: "All Americans deserve to have access to quality, affordable health care in their communities."
"Promote a vibrant, equitable economy. Invest in 21st century infrastructure."
"Prioritize education to provide opportunity for all."
Supports investing in renewable energy like wind and solar to reduce carbon pollution, and protecting New Mexico's water systems.
"We must protect and expand the benefits of Social Security and Medicare"; cosponsoring legislation to expand benefits and strengthen solvency.

H6NM03083.name: Martin Zamora
H6NM03083.bio: New Mexico State Representative for House District 63 since 2019, with a career in agriculture, cattle trading, fertilizer, steel and trucking.

positions.stance: Will defend private property rights, reduce burdensome federal regulations, and ensure agricultural producers have the tools they need.
Will champion pro-growth policies that lower taxes, cut red tape, and support small businesses.
Will stand with law enforcement and fight to restore law and order against crime and fentanyl.
"A nation without borders is not a nation"; calls the southern border crisis a threat to national security.

H6NM66015.name: Leanne Gandy
H6NM66015.bio: Former teacher and Superintendent of Lovington Schools; Director of Leadership Development for Cooperative Educational Services.

positions.stance: Will fight to lower the cost of living, promote good-paying local jobs, and reduce unnecessary regulations.
Will stand up to overregulation from Santa Fe and defend energy jobs and the families who depend on them.
Will defend water rights for farmers and ranchers and oppose burdensome regulations on agricultural producers.
Will focus on student outcomes, restore local control to school districts, and expand workforce and career training.
Believes decisions should be made locally, empowering school boards and pushing back against one-size-fits-all mandates.

H2NE01118.name: Mike Flood
H2NE01118.bio: U.S. Representative for Nebraska's 1st District; founder of Flood Communications and former Speaker of the Nebraska Legislature.

positions.stance: Voted to cut taxes, including No Tax on Tips, Overtime, and Social Security, and will keep backing policies that make life more affordable.
Voted to fund Border Patrol, border technology, and fighting fentanyl, and will keep supporting a secure border.
Launched Nebraska Backs the Blue and pledges to "always support the law enforcement officers" who keep Nebraskans safe.
Calls Communist China one of the greatest threats; works to keep Chinese technology off cell towers and stop CCP farmland purchases.
Voted for a rescission package and introduced the No More D.C. Waste Act to get federal spending under control.

H6NE01143.name: Chris Backemeyer
H6NE01143.bio: Former U.S. State Department official who served on the White House National Security Council and in the Office of the Vice President.

positions.stance: Supports a true public option for universal coverage, extending ACA premium tax credits, and protecting a woman's right to choose.
Supports strong border security, comprehensive reform with a pathway to citizenship, and clawing back excess ICE funding.
Supports a strong national defense, alliances through diplomacy, congressional war powers, and reversing VA cuts.
Supports ending tariff chaos, a long-term bipartisan Farm Bill, year-round E15, and breaking up agribusiness monopolies.
Supports rolling back tariffs, expanding the Child Tax Credit, making billionaires and corporations pay their fair share, and faster housing approvals.

H6NE02208.name: Brinker Harding
H6NE02208.bio: Omaha City Councilman since 2017 and business leader; former chief of staff to Omaha Mayor Hal Daub.

positions.stance: Will work to grow the economy, increase wages, keep inflation in check, and pass year-round E-15.
Will take on Big Pharma and Big Insurance so Americans pay the same low drug prices as other developed countries.
Will protect Social Security, Medicaid, and Medicare for single moms, veterans, the elderly, and disabled, "NOT illegal immigrants or able-bodied adults."
Supports term limits, banning congressional stock trading, and halting congressional salaries during shutdowns.
Supports body cameras and identifiable uniforms for ICE agents and deporting criminal illegal immigrants who commit violent crimes.

H6NE02174.name: Denise Powell
H6NE02174.bio: Small business owner and former corporate executive who founded an organization supporting Nebraskans running for local office.

positions.stance: Will work to stop tariffs, build affordable housing, keep healthcare premiums down, and invest in affordable childcare.
Supports Medicare drug price negotiation, a $35 insulin cap, a Medicare-like public option, and building on the Affordable Care Act.
Will fight to restore Roe v. Wade nationwide and to protect contraception and IVF access.
Will "Protect Social Security at all costs" and responsibly manage deficits and debts.
Supports fully funding police, reauthorizing the Violence Against Women Act, universal background checks, and red flag laws.

H6NE03115.name: Adrian Smith
H6NE03115.bio: U.S. Representative for Nebraska's Third District on the Ways & Means Committee.

positions.stance: Working with President Trump to "defeat the woke agenda and restore peace through strength."
Believes life begins at conception; opposes taxpayer-funded abortions and voted to end federal funding for Planned Parenthood.
Voted to finish the wall and increase Border Patrol funding, and supports ensuring only U.S. citizens can vote.
Helped write the 2017 Tax Cut and Jobs Act and the 2025 One Big Beautiful Bill making those tax cuts permanent.
Supports the Second Amendment and opposes new gun control measures.
Says labor unions "guarantee that hardworking Americans receive fair wages, safe and humane working conditions, and proper representation."
"I strongly support a woman's right to make her own healthcare decisions privately with her own doctor."
Supports equipping law enforcement officers with the necessary support, training, and resources to keep communities safe.
Supports a secure border while remembering the nation "has been, and always will be, a beacon of hope for all."
Supports respecting every law-abiding citizen's right to bear arms, paired with an equally strong commitment to preventing violence.

H8ID01124.name: Russ Fulcher
H8ID01124.bio: U.S. Representative from Idaho; former Idaho State Senator and Senate Republican Caucus Leader.

positions.stance: Supports strong border security, full enforcement of immigration law, and an orderly legal immigration process; opposes illegal immigration.
Strongly opposes breaching the lower four Snake River dams.
Proudly pro-life; believes life begins at conception and opposes taxpayer funding for abortion.
Opposes restrictions on gun rights and supports concealed carry reciprocity and lawful firearm ownership.
Believes local communities are better equipped to manage Idaho's forests, minerals, energy, and natural resources.
Supports banning congressional stock trades, term limits, overturning Citizens United, and campaign finance reform.
Describes herself as "a labor-first, union-first candidate"; supports middle-class tax relief, higher corporate taxes, and repealing "right to work."
"Idaho is not for sale"; seeks to permanently preserve Idaho's public lands with fully staffed and funded federal agencies.
Supports moving to a universal single-payer health care system.
Supports fully federally funding public education from pre-K through higher education and vocational training.

H8ID02064.name: Mike Simpson
H8ID02064.bio: U.S. Representative for Idaho's Second District on the House Appropriations Committee; former dentist.

positions.stance: Calls illegal immigration "the most important issue facing our nation"; fighting to build the wall and add border patrol agents.
Has made promoting Idaho agriculture one of his top priorities in Congress.
Opposes the Green New Deal as overreaching and ambiguous.
Committed to fulfilling the nation's obligations to veterans and fully funding the Veterans Administration.
Supports requiring a real photo ID for anyone who wants to vote, at the polls or by absentee ballot.

H8WV03097.name: Carol Miller
H8WV03097.bio: Member of Congress, small business owner, and farmer.

positions.stance: Lists "Protecting Coal & Gas" among her priorities.
Lists "Funding Education & Creating Jobs" among her priorities.
Lists "Supporting Farmers & Business" among her priorities.
Lists "Ending the Opioid Epidemic" among her priorities.
Lists "Defending the 2nd Amendment" among her priorities.

H6WV01160.name: Vince George
H6WV01160.bio: Public servant, former teacher, and community advocate.

positions.stance: Supports fully funding SNAP, Social Security, and veterans' benefits, and will fight to double the federal minimum wage.
Will fight to reverse cuts to Medicaid and Medicare and reduce the cost of health insurance.
Supports reallocating some military spending to improve West Virginians' lives, "not fund forever wars."
Supports mine safety, help for miners with black lung, holding coal companies accountable, and local say over data centers.
Says ICE is violating people's rights; will stand up for West Virginians' constitutional rights and due process.

H4WV02205.name: Riley Moore
H4WV02205.bio: U.S. Representative from West Virginia; former West Virginia State Treasurer (2021-2025) and state delegate.

positions.stance: Will "ALWAYS stand up for the rights of our citizens to keep and bear firearms."
Will stand up for West Virginia's coal and natural gas industries and their workers.
Pledges to keep fighting so "big business doesn't do big government's dirty work."
Believes in life from conception to natural death and will work "to end the tragedy of abortion."
Says "A zip code should not determine a child's future"; has fought for school choice and the Hope Scholarship.
Supports ending the current tariffs and having Congress exercise authority over tariffs, with all tariffs subject to public comment.
Supports ending the war with Iran and holding the administration accountable for war decisions under Congress's war powers.
Supports Small Business Administration grants and low-interest loans for West Virginia entrepreneurs and young people.
Supports a simpler, more transparent tax system with fewer loopholes "so that everybody pays their share."
For every $1 in wages lost when a factory or mine closes, will advocate investing $2 back into that community.

H2HI02128.name: Ed Case
H2HI02128.bio: U.S. Representative for Hawaii on the Appropriations Committee; lawyer and former Outrigger Hotels chief legal officer.

positions.stance: "We must forge a new way of governance that rejects pure partisan politics and incorporates our best ideas regardless of origin."
Supports terrorism prevention, a strong military, stronger intelligence capabilities, and supporting allies in the Asia-Pacific.
Supports constructive engagement with the world, especially the Indo-Pacific, and working with other countries on problem states.
Supports expanded legal immigration while curtailing illegal immigration, and affordable student loan programs.
"We must preserve and strengthen Social Security and Medicare and fulfill our commitments to our veterans and others."

H6HI01360.name: Adriel Lam
H6HI01360.bio: Retired after nearly 24 years of service in the U.S. Army.

H2HI02581.name: Jill Tokuda
H2HI02581.bio: U.S. Representative for Hawaii's Second Congressional District since 2022; former Hawaii State Senator.

positions.stance: Supports improved access to healthcare and mental health services and cosponsored the Medicare for All Act of 2023.
Fighting to suspend the federal gas tax, make childcare more affordable, and expand the Child Tax Credit and Earned Income Tax Credit.
"Aggressive action needs to be taken to address climate change impacts and increase renewable energy production."
Committed to securing federal disaster preparedness funding for first responders, governments, and community organizations.
Supports universal access to free, quality public education, including free community college and workforce training.
